tagline: Content categories with their own slots, so the mix stays balanced without discipline.
verdictSummary: SocialBee's organising idea is not the scheduler, it is the category: every post belongs to a bucket — educational, promotional, curated, personal — and each bucket owns specific slots in the week. The mix is then enforced by the schedule rather than by remembering. That is a genuinely different data model from a flat queue and it is a couple of days of work. The publishing half remains what it always is: one network per developer account and app review.
coreLoopDIY: Sort posts into content categories, give each category its own weekly slots, and let the schedule pull from the right bucket at the right time so the mix holds without thinking about it.
whatYouLose: every network beyond the one you got API approval for
the concierge service that writes and schedules for you
the analytics that tell you which category actually performs
whyPeopleStillPay: Because forty-nine dollars covers several networks at once, and each additional network in a personal build is another developer account and another review that may simply be refused.
notes: Category-driven slot allocation is the angle, deliberately distinct from the bulk-import-and-recycle approach taken by the other evergreen scheduler in this catalogue.
prompt:
Build a social scheduler organised around content categories rather than a flat queue.

Categories: a category has a name, a colour, a description of what belongs in it, and a recycling policy (post once and retire, or return to the pool after N days). Ship no categories; the first run asks the user to define theirs, since the mix is personal.

The schedule grid, which is the point of this build. The week is a grid of slots, and each slot is assigned to a category — Monday 09:00 educational, Monday 17:00 curated, Tuesday 09:00 educational, Wednesday 12:00 promotional. When a slot comes due, the scheduler takes the next eligible post from that category's pool. The mix over a month is therefore a property of the grid, not of the user's discipline, which is the entire idea.

Eligibility within a category: least-recently-posted first, skipping anything posted within its recycling interval, skipping anything whose media is missing, and skipping anything whose text is identical to something published within a configurable window. If a category's pool is empty when its slot comes due, leave the slot empty and warn — never borrow from another category, because silently filling an educational slot with a promotional post defeats the mechanism.

Health view: for each category, how many posts are in the pool, how many slots it holds per week, and how many weeks of runway that gives before it is exhausted. Show the projected published mix for the next month as a proportion per category, alongside the intended mix from the grid. A category with two posts and four slots a week is a problem visible three weeks before it becomes one.

Composer: character count against the connected network's real limit, media validation for size and aspect ratio, and a required category on every post.

Publishing: connect exactly one network through its documented OAuth flow with encrypted tokens and a visible reconnect flow. Publish through a background worker with idempotency keys, store the returned post ID, and surface failures with the platform's own error text. A failed post returns to the front of its category pool rather than being lost.

Bulk: import a CSV with a category column, and bulk-move posts between categories.

Out of scope: additional networks, scraping or unofficial APIs, analytics dashboards, team workspaces, and any AI generation of post text.

faq.q: Can I import my SocialBee content?
faq.a: Yes, and this is the cleanest migration in the category — SocialBee's export is CSV including the category, which is exactly the column this build needs. Media has to be downloaded and re-pathed, and posting history does not transfer.

faq.q: Why refuse to fill an empty slot from another category?
faq.a: Because the whole value is that the mix is guaranteed. A scheduler that quietly substitutes a promotional post when the educational pool runs dry produces exactly the drift the category system exists to prevent, and hides the fact that a pool needs refilling.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: A small VPS with PostgreSQL, five to ten dollars a month, plus local media storage. Against forty-nine dollars this is a large saving on paper, which evaporates if you needed the four extra networks that plan covers.

faq.q: What is the one thing that does not survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Reach across networks. The category model works just as well feeding five platforms as one, and this build feeds one. Every additional network is a separate developer account, a separate review, and a real possibility of refusal.
